ai.description: This snake reaches 60–90 cm. It is olive-brown with dark, checkered lateral spots and a distinct yellow or cream-colored nuchal collar. A dark subocular streak is a key diagnostic feature.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the presence of a distinct, narrow yellow or cream-colored collar behind the head, which is absent in other similar Indian keelback species.
ai.habitat: The St. John's Keelback inhabits freshwater wetlands, marshes, and paddy fields, typically found in low-to-mid altitude regions with dense aquatic vegetation.
ai.behavior: The St. John's Keelback is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on rocks or vegetation near water to regulate its body temperature before actively hunting for prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Fowlea sanctijohannis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–15 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, peaking between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Fowlea sanctijohannis* is endemic to the Western Himalayas, primarily occurring in Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand at elevations up to 2,000 meters.
